evidence: Return all tool_result blocks in one user message; if a tool fails, return its tool_result with is_error: true.

question:
An extraction service moves to claude-sonnet-5-5 and every request now fails with a 400 error. The team still needs tool arguments that always match the schema.
```python
resp = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5-5", max_tokens=1024,
    tools=[extract_invoice_tool],
    tool_choice={"type": "tool", "name": "extract_invoice"},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": doc_text}],
)
```
Which change fixes the request and keeps the guarantee?

options.A: Change the tool_choice type from tool to any, which lets Claude pick among the tools but still forces a call
options.B: Use tool_choice auto, set strict: true on the tool, and tell Claude in the prompt to call extract_invoice
options.C: Remove the tools and request JSON text that matches the schema, then parse it with json.loads
options.D: Keep the forced tool_choice and enable manual extended thinking with a budget so the model complies

rationale: Forced tool use (any or tool) is rejected on these models, so use auto with a prompt instruction that names the tool, and strict tool use to guarantee schema-valid arguments. (A) any is rejected as well. (C) drops the schema guarantee. (D) manual thinking budgets are not supported on current models and do not relax tool_choice.
evidence: On Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Fable 5.1, any and tool return a 400; use auto with strict tool use to guarantee schema-valid inputs.

question: A research assistant connects six MCP servers through the API's MCP connector, about 140 tools in all. Tool definitions consume roughly 60K tokens per request, and Claude often picks a similarly named tool from the wrong server. Which TWO changes address these problems? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Shorten every tool description to a few words so that the definitions use fewer tokens with each request it sends
options.B: Make one request per server and merge the answers in code, so that Claude never sees tools from two servers at once
options.C: Add the tool search tool and set defer_loading: true in each mcp_toolset default_config, keeping the busiest tools loaded
options.D: Allowlist the tools the assistant needs from each server: default_config enabled false, then enable chosen tools in configs
options.E: Turn on disable_parallel_tool_use so that only one tool is considered at a time during each turn of the conversation

rationale: Tool search with deferred loading keeps most definitions out of context until needed, which cuts the token bill, and an allowlist removes overlapping tools that cause wrong picks. (B) is an over-engineered workaround that loses cross-server reasoning. (A) removes the information Claude uses to choose. (E) parallel tool use controls how many calls happen at once, not how tools are selected.
evidence: Set defer_loading on the mcp_toolset default_config; allowlist by setting default_config enabled false and enabling specific tools in configs.

question: An engineering team builds one MCP server for its docs platform. Requirement 1: Claude must be able to open tickets on its own initiative. Requirement 2: the host application must be able to attach the current style guide as read-only context. Requirement 3: engineers want a reusable review this page workflow that they start explicitly. Which THREE designs map the requirements to the correct MCP primitives? (Select THREE.)

options.A: Expose the style guide as a resource with a URI, which the host application reads and attaches as context
options.B: Expose ticket creation as a tool with an input schema, so the model decides when to call it
options.C: Expose ticket creation as a resource, so the model can request the action by reading a URI
options.D: Expose the review workflow as a prompt template that the user selects, for example from a slash command
options.E: Expose the style guide as a prompt, so the model fetches it by invoking the prompt on demand

rationale: MCP separates model-controlled tools (actions the model chooses to call), application-controlled resources (data the host reads and attaches), and user-controlled prompts (templates a person invokes). (C) resources are read-only context, not actions. (E) prompts are chosen by the user, not fetched by the model on demand.
evidence: Tools are model-controlled, resources are application-controlled context, and prompts are user-controlled templates.

options.A: The tool returns a dict, but stdio can carry only strings; serialize the result with json.dumps first
options.B: print writes to stdout, which stdio reserves for protocol messages; log to stderr instead
options.C: The stdio transport cannot carry tools that take parameters; switch the server to the sse transport
options.D: The print call is not flushed, so protocol messages interleave; add flush=True to every print call

rationale: With stdio, the server's stdout carries only valid MCP messages, so a stray print corrupts the JSON-RPC stream; log to stderr. (A) the SDK serializes structured results itself. (C) stdio supports parameterized tools. (D) flushing the print still writes non-protocol text to stdout.
evidence: The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message; it may write logs to stderr.

question: A platform team wants a single MCP server for its deployment tooling, used by IDE agents on 300 laptops and by CI jobs. It must be upgraded centrally, and each caller must authenticate as themselves. Which setup fits?

options.A: Host it as a remote server over streamable HTTP and have each client authenticate with its own OAuth token
options.B: Expose it over a raw WebSocket on a custom port, since MCP clients negotiate WebSocket by default
options.C: Run it over stdio on a bastion host and tunnel each client's input and output over SSH using one shared account
options.D: Ship the server binary to every laptop and CI runner as a stdio subprocess with a shared key in its environment

rationale: A centrally hosted, remote server needs a network transport; streamable HTTP is the standard one, and it works with per-user OAuth authorization. (D) stdio servers run per client, so upgrades are distributed and the identity is shared. (C) tunnels a local transport and still shares one account. (B) the standard transports are stdio and streamable HTTP, not WebSocket.
evidence: The standard MCP transports are stdio (client-launched subprocess) and Streamable HTTP (independent server, HTTP POST/GET).

question: A docs team wants Claude to follow its release-notes procedure: a six-step checklist, a Markdown template, and a short script that lints the result. Nothing external is queried, and the procedure should load only when someone asks for release notes. What is the best fit?

options.A: An MCP server whose tools return the checklist and template and run the lint script remotely
options.B: A system prompt section with the full procedure, included in every session the team starts
options.C: A Skill that bundles the checklist, template, and lint script, loaded on demand
options.D: A custom tool in each application that returns the template text whenever Claude requests it

rationale: A Skill packages instructions and scripts and loads them progressively, only when the task matches. (A) adds a server to deploy and secure for a procedure that touches no external system. (D) must be rebuilt in every application and covers only the template. (B) spends tokens in every session whether or not release notes are requested.
evidence: Skills are folders of instructions and scripts loaded on demand through progressive disclosure, based on the Skill's name and description.

question: A billing application needs Claude to compute shipping quotes. The logic is a function in the application's own codebase, uses the current request's database session, and no other product will ever call it. How should it be exposed?

options.A: As an MCP connector entry pointing at the application's localhost address, with the quote function behind it
options.B: As a standalone MCP server with its own deployment, so other clients can reuse the function later
options.C: As a Skill whose script Claude runs, passing the live database session into it as an argument
options.D: As a custom tool in the request, run by the app when a tool_use block for it arrives

rationale: A function that lives in the app and needs its in-process state is best a custom tool executed by the application loop. (B) is over-engineering for a single consumer and cannot see the request's session. (A) the connector requires a publicly reachable HTTPS server, so localhost does not work. (C) a script cannot receive a live in-process session object.
evidence: Custom tools are app-specific functions executed in your loop; the MCP connector needs a public HTTP server and cannot reach local servers.

question: A developer wants Claude to use a vendor's remote MCP server through the Messages API. Requirement 1: the server's tools must be available to Claude in the request. Requirement 2: the server requires OAuth. Which TWO actions are needed? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Declare the server with a command and args so the API launches it as a local subprocess
options.B: Let the API run the OAuth sign-in flow for the user and store the resulting tokens for later requests
options.C: Add an mcp_toolset entry to tools whose mcp_server_name matches the server's name in mcp_servers
options.D: Obtain and refresh the OAuth access token in the application and pass it as authorization_token
options.E: Rely on the connector to expose the server's resources and prompts to Claude alongside its tools

rationale: The connector needs both a server definition in mcp_servers and a matching mcp_toolset in tools, and the caller handles OAuth, obtaining and refreshing the token. (A) local stdio servers cannot be connected through the connector. (B) the API does not run the OAuth flow. (E) only tool calls are supported, not resources or prompts.
evidence: Every server in mcp_servers must be referenced by one mcp_toolset; API consumers handle the OAuth flow and pass authorization_token.

options.A: Project-scoped files cannot hold stdio servers started with npx; move the entry to each developer's user config
options.B: The metrics entry cannot live in the file; it must be added with the claude mcp add command on each machine
options.C: A database credential is committed in plain text; reference ${DATABASE_URL} so each developer supplies it from their environment
options.D: The two servers use different transports, so Claude Code rejects the file; convert both to stdio command entries
